title: From Minimal Innate Skills to Open-Ended Competence: Autonomous Knowledge Expansion for Lifelong Robots
content: Autonomous robots should continuously extend what they can learn rather than remain limited to a fixed set of predefined tasks and skills. However, existing learning systems typically optimize within predetermined task, data, or capability spaces and provide limited mechanisms for making new learning opportunities themselves reachable. This paper proposes an autonomous reachable learning space expansion model in which newly acquired knowledge and skills progressively enlarge the space of future learnable knowledge. The model maintains persistent learning beyond individual tasks and expands learning along environmental, temporal, and thinking dimensions. Environmental interaction exposes previously inaccessible observations and opportunities, temporal accumulation enables delayed and long-term relations to be learned, and thinking generates new candidate problems through abstraction, transfer, combination, and variation. Newly acquired capabilities are recursively reused to unlock further learning opportunities, while an online learning process adapts which materials should receive priority. Experiments show that the full model increases structural diversity from 0.740 to 0.947, raises reachable scope from 19.70 to 29.60 over random exploration, and improves cumulative learning utility from 124.99 to 148.38 over a fixed priority strategy.
